missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-feller-bernstein-hausdorff-C016 (partial): The hypotheses are not plainly stated. Body line 345 reads 'positive black weight b, red weight r and same-color reinforcement c>0'. That wording puts a positivity condition on b and c but none on the red weight r. The conclusion that the c_n are 'precisely the moments of beta(b/c,r/c)', which Hausdorff uniqueness then uses to identify the mixing law, needs r>0. The handbook defines beta(alpha,beta) only for alpha,beta>0 (def:p15-beta-integral), and the cited exchangeability theorem thm:p15-polya-word-law assumes r>0. At r=0 the formula gives c_n=1, which are the moments of delta_1, and no beta law exists. So r>0 is an unstated assumption on the plain reading. Every other element is present: the product and gamma forms of c_n, the empty-product convention, the beta moments, the Hausdorff identification, the word and count probabilities, and agreement with the direct urn law (body 344-358, annex 555-584, held Feller II PDF pp. 244-245 = printed 229-230).
